When does reconstruction hold up?

Vary the number of measurements and the noise. Compare the inverse PINN with a network without a PDE loss and an analytical fit — using exactly the same observations.

How to read the benchmark

Velocity: hidden-phase RMSE divided by the fixed velocity scale 1.5. Flow and wall shear: full-cycle relative L2 errors. All are expressed as percentages; their definitions differ.

Noise is Gaussian with a standard deviation of 0%, 3%, 10% or 20% of 1.5, not of each local velocity. Increasing the measurement count adds nested radial locations at six fixed observed phases. Each seed changes both observation noise and neural initialization.

Both networks use the same architecture, periodic time features, exact centre symmetry and no-slip wall conditions. The data-only network omits the differential-equation loss. Both receive 1,000 Adam steps and up to 100 L-BFGS iterations; this is an equal iteration budget, not equal runtime.

The analytical fit knows the correct harmonic solution family. Geometry, frequency and α = 3 are known. These results describe a favourable synthetic benchmark, not clinical validation or universal superiority of one method. Three seeds give preliminary variability estimates, not confidence intervals.

Timing caveat: the pilot ran sequentially and the remaining cases used up to three concurrent CPU processes. These times include contention and are not a controlled speed benchmark.
